ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are two rows of activity order for nitration reactions of aromatic compounds connected by “<”. Row (1) in order is a benzene ring bearing -CO2H, a benzene ring bearing -CH2CH3, and a benzene ring bearing -OH, representing -CO2H < -CH2CH3 < -OH. Row (2) in order is a benzene ring bearing -CO2H, a benzene ring bearing -NHC2H5, a benzene ring bearing -NH2, and a benzene ring bearing -NO2, representing -CO2H < -NHC2H5 < -NH2 < -NO2. Then reason: In nitration reactions, substituents on the aromatic ring have a great influence on reaction activity. -CO2H is an electron-withdrawing group, making the benzene ring deactivated and the nitration activity relatively low; alkyl groups such as -CH2CH3 have a weak electron-donating effect and can weakly activate the benzene ring; -OH has a strong electron-donating effect and can strongly activate the benzene ring. Therefore, in (1), the activity order from low to high, -CO2H < -CH2CH3 < -OH, is correct. In (2), nitrobenzene substituted with -NO2 is placed at the far right, which is equivalent to considering its nitration activity the highest, but -NO2 is a strong electron-withdrawing and strongly deactivating group; nitrobenzene should be harder to nitrate than benzene and should not be placed at the highest-activity end, so (2) is incorrect. Therefore the correct expression is (1).

method.method_draft: After reading the compounds in the image, evaluate each proposed sequence mechanistically. In row (1), -CO2H withdraws electron density and destabilizes the arenium ion, ethyl donates weakly through hyperconjugation, and -OH donates strongly by resonance, so the depicted increasing ease of nitration is mechanistically consistent. In row (2), -NO2 withdraws very strongly by both induction and resonance, so nitrobenzene should be among the least reactive, not placed at the highest-reactivity end. Hence row (2) is invalid and the correct expression is (1).
